component.name: Todav
component.summary: Tasks and calendar kept in your Nextcloud

description.p: Todav is a task list and calendar kept in your Nextcloud through CalDAV, so the Nextcloud Tasks and Calendar web apps and other CalDAV clients see the same lists and events.

ul.li: Works offline; changes sync when the server is reachable
Changes from other devices arrive within seconds through push
Categories, subtasks, due dates and reminders
Month, week and agenda views; plan tasks into time slots by drag and drop
An optional GNOME Shell extension, installed separately, puts your tasks and calendar in the top bar
Connects through GNOME Online Accounts or a browser sign-in

screenshot.caption: Tasks grouped by category, with subtasks and due dates
The month, with an event's details
Tasks planned into the week next to events

ul.li: GNOME extension: its D-Bus proxy is created when the extension is enabled and its pending request is cancelled when it is disabled (extensions.gnome.org review).

Linux: a "+" beside Categories in the Tasks sidebar adds a category (it shows even for a list without any), and a right-click or long press on a category offers Edit… to rename it on all the list's tasks, as one undo step.
Linux: dropping a task in a long list with manual sorting no longer freezes the window for seconds; the page is rebuilt once after a burst of changes instead of once per renumbered task.

Notes of tasks and events in light Markdown: bold, italic, headings, lists and code show formatted; links, bare web addresses, e-mail addresses and todav:// links open with a click (Ctrl+click while editing on Linux); checkboxes (- [ ]) tick with a click, also in an item's details. Notes stay plain text, so other apps show them as written.

Join Call for an event's video call (Google Meet, Zoom, Teams, Jitsi, Webex, Nextcloud Talk and others), found in its link, place or notes: in its details, its reminder and the GNOME extension's agenda.
Linux: Snooze on task and event reminders, back in ten minutes, as on Android.
Week numbers in the calendar (the months and the week views) and, by a setting of their own, in the GNOME extension's month and the month widget; both off by default.
Cancelled events and invitations you declined (found by your addresses on the server) show as usual, crossed out (the default) or not at all, by a setting; declined ones remind no more.
Export a task list or a calendar to an iCalendar file (.ics), from its dialog: everything in it, done tasks too.
Duplicate a task with its subtasks, or an event (the whole series, without its attendees), from its dialog or its details; Undo takes the copy back.

Linux: Ctrl while dropping a task or an event on another list or calendar in the sidebar copies it there instead of moving it; the pointer shows a copy. Events of read-only calendars drag too, to be copied that way.
Android: the agenda widget's title can be hidden, by a setting of the widget; its buttons then float over the agenda's top corner.
Android: the agenda widget's rows show an event's place under its title, and its time on the right with its length under it (as "1h 30m").
An online meeting's place (an event with a video call link) shows with a camera instead of a map pin: in its details on Linux and Android and in the agenda widget.
Android: a widget's row, item or day shows it is pressed, in a grey that stands out on light and dark backgrounds.
Android: the calendar's month shows as much of a title as fits rather than its first word only, so birthdays ("🎂 Name") show the name, not only the cake.
Android: an event opened from a widget opens over the calendar on its day, so Back leads there rather than to the tasks.

Android: the widgets move on to the new day at midnight (and when the clock or the time zone changes), the day widget's line at the current time every quarter hour; a widget's settings show on it even when left right after the change.
Linux: Edit… in an item's details in the calendar opens it as it is now, with a title or note changed there meanwhile.
Android: the calendar's day list no longer crashes on two items of the same title at the same time in one list.
Linux: Todav no longer crashes when Preferences close after an account was added, moved or switched on or off in them.
Events in light colours (white, yellow…) show their titles in dark text instead of white, in the app and the calendar widgets; so do the colour swatches' checks.
Linux: the calendar's Month view no longer scrolls back month after month without end when it is redrawn (an event saved after editing, an undo) while one of its items has the focus.
The GNOME Shell extension runs on GNOME 48 too (Debian 13, for instance), with the app installed as a Flatpak.

A server whose certificate comes from a certificate authority added to the system (a self-hosted Nextcloud's own CA) connects, instead of failing with "invalid peer certificate: UnknownIssuer": Todav trusts the system's certificate authorities, not only its built-in list; on Android the ones installed by the user too.
An error page from the server or a proxy shows as its text in error messages, not as its HTML.
The GNOME extension no longer fills the system log with "Attempting to call back into JSAPI during the sweeping phase of GC", one per task row, after a task is added or the list is changed.

Repeating tasks: Repeat in a task's dialog (daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, every n of them, until a day), counted from its start or else its due date, or from the day it is done (Repeat From Completion). Ticked, it moves on to its next date, missed ones skipped, with its reminders and its subtasks open again; at the end of its rule it is completed. Repeating tasks from other apps move on the same way (before, ticking one completed the whole series). An arrow by the due date marks them.
Calendars subscribed to by link in Nextcloud (New subscription from link: a published Outlook or Google calendar, holidays…) show as read-only calendars, updated when Nextcloud refreshes its copy.

Preferences > Calendar > Tasks for other calendars' events: a task list for tasks of events of calendars that hold no tasks (subscriptions, shared calendars you may only view, the phone's); with None, the default, those events take no tasks.
Linux: an event's edit dialog lists its tasks, to tick or add one, as its details do.

Linux: a click on a day of the month view, or a drag across days, offers a new all-day event over them in a popover, as GNOME Calendar does: its title, colour and calendar, then Add, or Edit… for the whole dialog with what was typed. A double click still opens the dialog.
Android: holding a day of the month opens a new all-day event on it, and holding then moving across days, on it over all of them (holding an event still moves it).

A task ticked done that leaves the list (into its Completed group, out of Upcoming or Important, a completed subtask hidden) stays where it was, struck through, for a moment, then fades out, on Linux and Android, in the GNOME extension's task list and the task widget (in steps there); ticking several in a row, they all stay until the last one's moment is over.

Android: haptic feedback where it helps: a bump when something is held to move, a tick for each day, time step or place it is moved across and when it is dropped there; when a swipe, a pull to sync or a sheet goes far enough to act; ticking a task and every switch on or off, felt as such (a task's every check box, the calendars to show, the settings); picking a priority; reaching the sidebar's narrowest or widest.
Android: System Calendars can be renamed and recoloured, in Todav only; "Use the System's Name and Color" in the same dialog undoes it.

An event's own colour, shown instead of its calendar's in every view, the widgets and the extension: one set in Nextcloud Calendar or Thunderbird (COLOR), or with the colour box by its title, in its details (saved at once) and its dialog (Linux) or page (Android): its calendar's colour, 12 colours or any other. It is saved as the closest CSS colour name, as Nextcloud Calendar saves it. On Android, a System Calendar's event shows its own colour too (Google Calendar's event colours).
Android: any colour for a list or calendar, with Custom Color after the presets, as on Linux.

Android: the calendar's Today button left the top bar for a small floating button above the add button, shown only while the calendar is away from today: another day picked, or today scrolled out of sight.

A task added for an event goes to the event's calendar, and only calendars that hold tasks offer to add one, unless a list is picked for the others (before, any event took tasks, added to the last opened list).
A new event added in the month view (the add button, Ctrl+N, a month widget's add button) is all-day, as one added by a double click on a day of the month already was on Linux.
Android: an event lasting several days is one bar across them in the month view and the Day view's week, as in the Linux app and the widget, instead of a chip on each day.

In the month view, what does not fit on a day is counted at its top right ("+2", which lists it on Linux) instead of taking the day's last row, so an event lasting several days shows from its first day as a whole bar even where a day is full. On Linux the day's number moved to the left for it, as on Android.

Moving an event's start in its dialog (Linux) or page (Android) leaves its end where it is, as GNOME Calendar does; only a start past the end takes it along. Before, the end moved with the start, keeping the event's length.

A sync that fails on a server's answer that is not valid XML says which request it was and where the answer broke ("Sync failed: parse: PROPFIND /remote.php/dav/...: ..., byte N of M, after ..."), to find what sent it.
Android: On This Device Only comes last among the accounts to add, after System Calendars.
An older Todav no longer opens data a newer one left (after a downgrade, say); it says to update instead of reading and writing a database it does not know.
Linux: the sidebar month no longer marks days with dots unless "Dots in the sidebar month" is turned on in Preferences.
Android: the keyboard starts each word of an event's location with a capital letter.
A green icon instead of the blue one, on Linux and Android; Android's colours without the system's own (before Android 12), the widgets' own colours and the launcher shortcuts are green with it.

Linux: editing an item and adding an event on a day of the month by a double click, with the "Edit on double click" setting. A click shows an item's details or a day's new event popover at once, with Edit there; a double click on a free hour of the week view still adds an event.
Android: Enter in a task's or an event's title closes the keyboard instead of starting a new line, which made the title two lines.
Android: an event's or a task's block in the week views shows as many whole lines of its title as fit, the last one ending in "…", instead of a line cut in half.
Android: on wide screens a message (with Undo, say) shows at the bottom of the view, beside the add button, instead of in the middle of the window over the rail and the sidebar.
Android: a new message (with Undo, say) takes the place of the one shown instead of waiting for it: a few actions in a row kept messages on screen for minutes.
Linux: a long description or title in an event's or a task's details wraps instead of making the popover as wide as the window.
Linux: a list's Completed group stays open when a task in it is reopened or the list is redrawn, until it is closed.
Linux: every task list is as wide at a given window size; one with a long row was a little wider than the others.
Linux: the week views' title names the month in the form a date takes ("16 – 22 listopada 2026" in Polish, not "listopad").
Linux: in an event's or a task's details, the text of every line starts at the same place, after an icon, the calendar's dot or the colour box alike.
Linux: an event's place shows by a map pin in every icon theme; some (Tela) drew it as a black disc.
Linux: deleting an event or a task from its details in the month view, or editing it from there, no longer scrolls the month away.
About one push message in 256 failed with "Sync failed: parse: ill-formed document": an encrypted one that happened to start like XML was read as XML instead of being decrypted.
Android: Undo after completing a task with a swipe brought it back only to complete it again at once.
Android: on a phone, saving a new event after typing its title showed the task list under the Calendar button, until Tasks and Calendar were tapped again.
Android: saving an event saved it as it was at the first change made on its page and dropped the changes after it, such as a repeat picked after the title was edited.
Android: a message with Undo ("... saved", "... completed") stayed until swiped away, and the messages after it waited behind it; it now goes after ten seconds.
Deleting a task deletes its subtasks too, and one Undo brings them all back; before, they stayed behind, under a task that was gone.

A task's reminder goes away once the task is done, moved on to its next date or deleted, here or on another device; before, it stayed until dismissed. "Mark as Done" on a reminder that no longer applies does nothing, so a repeating task does not move on twice.

Google Tasks in the Google account (Linux, through GNOME Online Accounts): its task lists show next to its calendars and sync with Google, checked every minute while the window is focused and every 30 minutes otherwise. Task lists can be added, renamed and deleted there; their colours stay on each device. Google keeps a task's title, notes, done, a due date without a time, subtasks and order only, so the edit dialog offers just those, rows have no star or pin, and the calendar plans these tasks onto days, not into hours.
Fedora packages on COPR (selfref/todav), built with each release.

Reminders for a task's start, set below its start date in the edit dialog (Linux) or the task page (Android), next to the due date's; their notification says when the task starts. Start reminders from other apps (such as Tasks.org's "when started") show there too, instead of as the due date's.
Priority on events, as on tasks (none, low, medium or high), set in the event dialog (Linux) or page (Android) and shown in its details; the same iCalendar priority Thunderbird sets.

Urgent reminders for important tasks and events (high priority): on Linux they stay on screen until dismissed, on Android they come on a channel of their own ("Urgent reminders"), which can have its own sound or get through Do Not Disturb. "Urgent reminders for all" in Preferences → General → Notifications (Settings → General on Android), off by default, makes every reminder urgent.
A task reminder whose time had already passed when it was set (a task due in 10 minutes, reminded 15 minutes before) now goes off at once, instead of never, while the task is still ahead.
Linux: reminders go off on time, not up to 30 seconds later.
Android: the task page showed a task's reminders as a long custom time span, and saving the task moved them years ahead; it shows and keeps them as set now.

Checking off tasks outside the app, off by default: a task's circle completes or reopens it in the GNOME extension (Preferences → Extension → Tasks → Check off tasks; in the task list and the agenda) and in Android's task and agenda widgets (each widget's settings → Check Off Tasks). Subtasks follow as Settings → Tasks say, when they would be asked about: then they stay as they are.

A sort button next to Search on the task page picks the task order. Settings → Tasks → Sort is now Sort at start: the last used (the default, so the order picked last stays), or one the app sorts by whenever it opens.
Linux: a task's context menu in "To Plan" can delete it too (with Undo), next to Edit….

Settings → General → Default App → Calendar: the system's calendar app, with a button making it Todav. On Linux it does so at once (the app opening calendar files, which GNOME takes as its calendar app; not in the Flatpak). On Android, which lets no app do that, the system asks which app (Todav, then Always); another app's default is cleared first in its "Open by default" settings, which the button opens.

Extension: its parts can go in GNOME's clock menu, the month in place of its calendar and the agenda in place of its events, with the task list under them. Preferences → Extension shows the two ways with pictures, Todav's icon with its own menu (with fields for adding) or the clock menu (with buttons), and Custom for each part (the task list, the month, the agenda) in either menu or nowhere. The icon shows only with something in its menu.

Extension: Preferences → Extension → Adding tasks and Adding events: a field (as before), a button opening Todav (in the list's field for adding a task, or on a new event on the day picked), or none; with the task list, and with the agenda (else the month).
Extension: Preferences → Extension → Number by the icon: the open tasks of the list shown (as before), tasks due today or earlier, important tasks, today's events, or none.
Extension: Preferences → Extension → Order puts the calendar before the tasks in its own menu (on the left in two columns, on top in one).
Extension: a right click on its icon opens a menu with Open Todav and Preferences (Todav's, on the Extension page).
Android: a low month planner widget shows slimmer bars, as Fossify Calendar's, before none.
Android: a list or calendar held in the sidebar to move it rises off it, with a shadow.
Android: a task held to move rises as soon as the long press is felt, not once it moves.
Android: a tap anywhere on the task widget but a task or a button opens its list in the app, not only on its name.
Extension: its icon sits in the middle of the top bar, next to the clock; Preferences → Extension → Icon puts it back on the right.
Extension: a day clicked in the month shows that day in the agenda, and an event added then starts on it; a double click opens it in Todav (one click, without the agenda in sight).

Extension: Preferences → Extension → Open in the editor, for tasks and for events: a task or an event clicked (in the task list or the agenda) opens in its editor in Todav, rather than in its list or on its day. Off by default.
Android: "Mark as Done" on a reminder completes the task's subtasks too when Settings → Tasks say so (Completing a task with open subtasks: Completes them too), as on Linux.
Android: the month planner widget's weeks fill it to the bottom, also where the launcher says it is smaller than it is.
Android: a task dragged off the middle of a row, down past it, lands below that row rather than staying set to become its subtask.
Android: in a sorted list, a task dragged over another moves no rows aside (a drop there makes it a subtask, highlighting that row, and reorders nothing).
Linux: a task dragged beside another in a sorted list says why it cannot go there (set Sort to Manual), as on Android.
Linux: Saturdays and Sundays tinted red a little in the calendar's day names and numbers, and in the sidebar's month, as on Android.
Tasks whose subtasks are shown stay so after a restart, on each device.

Linux: the month view scrolls up and down a week at a time, as GNOME Calendar's, by the mouse wheel (a week per notch), a touchpad or a touchscreen; the arrows, Today and a day in another month scroll there smoothly.

Android: the month view scrolls up and down a week at a time, as GNOME Calendar's, instead of swiping a month sideways; a mouse wheel scrolls it a week per notch, and Today or a day in another month scrolls there.
Android: the month planner widget can be made as low as the month widget; low, it shows each week's days with as many bars as fit, down to none.
Calendar: Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+6 open the views in the menu's order: Month, Week, Work Week, 3 Days, Day, Agenda (Agenda moves from Ctrl+3 to Ctrl+6).
Android: pulling a task's details up while adding a subtask goes on in the editor's Add Subtask, with what was typed and the cursor; back down, the text is still there.
Android: a widget resized on the home screen is laid out for its new size at once, not only when it next updates.
Android: Add Subtask in a task's details stays above the keyboard; with many subtasks it was hidden under it.
Android: the arrows of the calendar widgets turn the month or day again; in release builds they did nothing.
Linux: About shows when a newer stable version is out on GitHub, with a link to its release.
Flatpak: Todav no longer asks for access to the system keyring; it keeps its passwords through the Secret portal, as it already did.
Android: the APK in the releases is signed with Todav's own key, so later versions install over it. Coming from 2.0.1 or earlier, uninstall the old one first, one last time.
Android: Todav is in English when English comes first in the system's languages, not in the next language it has a translation for.

Linux: Todav can be the system's calendar app (Settings → Apps → Default Apps → Calendar): it opens iCalendar files (.ics), whose events and tasks go into the calendar and task list picked for them; an item already there is replaced.

Android: Todav can be the calendar other apps and the system open: at a time or an event of the system's calendars (clocks, At a Glance: their day), for other apps' "Add to calendar" (a new event with what they give), and for iCalendar files opened or shared (imported, as on Linux). Copy Link on a task's page and in a task's or an event's details gives a todav:// link that opens it.
Android: "New Event" next to "New Task" on the launcher icon, a Quick Settings tile for a new task, and Snooze on reminders (back in ten minutes).
Linux: open tasks and events whose titles hold what is typed show in the Activities overview's search; one opens on its list or day, the app's heading searches its tasks in Todav.

Linux: Copy Link in a task's or an event's dialog and in their details on the calendar puts a todav:// link on the clipboard; pasted elsewhere (notes, a chat), it opens the item in Todav: a task on its list, an event on its day.

Linux: Google calendars, through a Google account in GNOME Online Accounts: their events show, sync and can be edited, and the calendars renamed and recoloured; their order stays on this device. Google keeps no task lists, and calendars are added and deleted in Google Calendar. Only Nextcloud is fully supported, as adding one says; one whose sign-in gave no access to the calendars is not added, with what to do instead.

Android: System Calendars, on the welcome page and in Settings → Accounts → Add Account, shows the calendars of the device's own accounts (Google, Exchange, DAVx⁵…), read-only. None is shown at first; each is turned on in the account's page, and changes to them show up at once. One Todav already syncs itself (DAVx⁵'s copy of a Nextcloud calendar, say) is marked "Already in Todav", as its events would show twice. With nowhere to add a list, calendar, task or event (only these calendars), the add buttons are not shown.
A read-only calendar's events can no longer be changed, rather than the server refusing the change later; on Android their details no longer offer Edit and Delete.

Android: a full Material 3 Expressive app. Tasks and Calendar switched by a navigation bar on phones and a rail on wider screens, whose menu button shows the lists and calendars: a page of its own on phones, a sidebar that can be hidden and resized on unfolded foldables and tablets; a task page with everything the Linux edit dialog has; swipe actions picked in Settings for each direction (complete, star, pin or delete with Undo); drag tasks to reorder them, make them subtasks or change their category; month, week and agenda views where events and tasks move by dragging; an event editor with repeating events; "To Plan" for putting tasks into hours of the week; search; settings and accounts; reminders; push through UnifiedPush; "New Task" from the launcher; adding shared text as a task; keyboard shortcuts.

Android: home-screen widgets, read-only as the GNOME extension: a task list (or Upcoming, Important) by category with its subtasks, the month with a dot per calendar on each day, the coming week's agenda, a day's hours, and a month planner with bars across the days. A task or an event opens in its editor (on the month planner, the day tapped), a month's or day's title in the calendar. Each has an add button and settings (its list, or calendars other than those shown in the app; its add button), in the launcher's menu of the widget and in Settings → Widgets, which also sets their colours (the system's, or a background and a text colour for light and dark), the background's opacity, the corners' radius and a settings button on each widget.
Android: Saturdays and Sundays tinted red a little in the calendar's day names and numbers, and in the month widgets'.

Android: a launcher icon of its own, the calendar page filling whatever shape the launcher gives icons, with a themed version; the app opens on it over the system's accent colour, light or dark with it.
Android: About Todav in Settings has a Support section with the Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors and Liberapay links, as About on Linux.
Android: an account of the Nextcloud app on the device fills in the server and login name of a sign-in.
Android: each release has an APK, a test build until Google Play and F-Droid: uninstall the previous one before installing the next.

Calendar: Work Week, 3 Days and Day views. Work Week shows the days picked in Preferences (Monday to Friday at first); 3 Days moves a day at a time; Day shows its week above the hours. Ctrl+4, Ctrl+5 and Ctrl+6 open them. On Linux the views are now picked from a menu.
Calendar: an event's or a task's title can be changed right in its details popover: click it, type, press Enter.

Lists and calendars can be put in any order by dragging them in the sidebar, within their account; with Nextcloud the order is shared with its Calendar and Tasks apps and other devices, lists on this device keep theirs here. On Android, hold a list, then drag it.
Linux: the sidebar can be hidden with the button at the start of the header or F9; in a narrow window it opens over the content instead of in place of it.
Calendar: clicking a task in "To Plan" says how to plan it: drag it onto the calendar; right-clicking it offers Edit….
Calendar: in the agenda, as in the GNOME extension, a task is a ring in its list's colour, with a tick when done, and an event a dot; a task is ticked in its details, not in the agenda.
Android: signing in with the browser no longer fails with "Login failed" when Android cuts off Todav's network while the browser is in front.
On a new installation, reminders never went off.
The calendar no longer highlights the first day of a month or week moved to with the arrows as if it had been picked.
Calendar: a task or event dragged over the events of a day lights the day up, as over its free space.

"Completing a task with open subtasks" in Preferences > Tasks: completing a task completes its open subtasks too (the default, as in Nextcloud Tasks; reopening a subtask then reopens its task), leaves them open, or asks each time.
Reopening a task with completed subtasks asks whether they reopen too.
"Edit titles in place" in Preferences > Tasks: a click on a task's title with a mouse or touchpad edits it right in the list. Off by default.
When Todav is updated while it runs, it restarts into the new version by itself if its window is closed, and otherwise offers Restart in a banner.
The open subtasks of a completed task stay under it among the open tasks instead of showing as top-level tasks.
Undoing a change while a sync was uploading it no longer gets the change back from the server: a task reopened that way was completed again a moment later.

Several accounts side by side: more Nextcloud accounts (through GNOME Online Accounts or signed in in Todav, on the same server or others) and the lists kept on this device, each an account in Preferences → Accounts. Add one with Add; each has its own page with its name, its connection, Server Status and Remove. The sidebars and list pickers group lists by account, in the order set by dragging the accounts by their handles.
An account can be switched off: its lists and calendars are hidden and stop syncing, nothing is deleted.
"Sync settings with" in Preferences → Accounts picks the account settings sync through, or none. The welcome page asks whether to sync settings with the account added there.
A banner over the tasks and the calendar names an account that is not connected (its password is gone from the keyring, or its GNOME Online Accounts account), with Sign In.
The lists on this device are an account of their own ("On This Device"), replacing the "Local lists and calendars" switch; hidden local lists stay hidden, as a switched-off account.
An account without its password no longer shows the welcome page: its lists stay usable and the banner offers to sign in again.

Signing in to a server offers its three ways as buttons (with the browser, by a copied login link, with a password) instead of a button with a menu; while the browser sign-in waits, only Cancel shows.
Signing in again keeps the account: a different user is added as another account, and a GNOME Online Accounts account and a sign-in in Todav are separate accounts rather than one switch.
A calendar new on the server, or every calendar of an account just added, gets DAV Push at the sync that finds it instead of up to an hour later.
About has a Support page with where to support Todav's development: Ko-fi, GitHub Sponsors and Liberapay.

Server Status in Preferences → Accounts: the Nextcloud version (or why the server cannot be reached, or that it is in maintenance mode), when Todav last synced, and whether DAV Push works. Without DAV Push on the server, it says what that means and links to the app in the Nextcloud App Store; with it but no ntfy server, it asks for one.
Extension: a settings button in the Extensions app, opening Todav's Preferences on the Extension page.
An RPM spec for Fedora, with the extension as a separate package, built on COPR from .copr/Makefile.
Todav uses the system's SQLite library instead of a built-in copy; packages now depend on it.
The app's store listing has screenshots, release notes and brand colours, and says the GNOME Shell extension is optional and installed separately.
A task's subtask count ("1/4") counts only its own subtasks; deeper ones count on their subtask's row.
Extension: with tasks and calendar side by side, the task list and the agenda take the height their column has to spare, so the fields for adding a task and an event line up.
An account whose password is missing no longer reports "Sync failed: no account configured" in local mode; Preferences say it is not connected, and signing in again reconnects it.
Extension: hovering over the menu no longer highlights all of it with themes that style hovered menu items, such as Blur my Shell's; only the row under the pointer is highlighted.
The app ID is now dev.aperte.Todav and the extension's UUID todav@aperte.dev. Todav moved to AperteDev on GitHub.
Use Todav without an account: "On This Device Only" on the welcome page keeps your task lists and calendars on this computer, starting with a task list and a calendar.

"Local lists and calendars" in Preferences → Accounts: keep lists and calendars on this device only, next to the synced ones. Turning it off hides them; nothing is deleted. New lists and calendars ask where to go.
The sidebars and the event dialog's calendar picker group lists and calendars by where they are kept, those on this device last.
Move tasks to another list and events to another calendar by dropping them on it in the sidebar; a task takes its subtasks along.
A list picker in the task dialog, to move a task to another list.
A star on every task, coloured by its priority; its menu sets the priority. As in Nextcloud Tasks, a starred task is one of high priority.
An Important page with the high-priority tasks of every list.
"Priority, highest first" to sort tasks and subtasks.
Pin tasks to the top of their list, in a Pinned group (shared with Nextcloud Tasks' pins).
"Stars" and "Pins" in Preferences → Tasks turn either off; pinned tasks stay pinned for other apps.

Nested subtasks, any number of levels deep: a subtask's "+" adds subtasks to it, and a task dropped on a "+" moves there with its own subtasks; dropped on an "Add subtask" field, it goes where a new subtask would. The task details on the calendar list a subtask's subtasks too.
The welcome page asks first how to use Todav (GNOME Online Accounts, a Nextcloud server or this device only), then for the account.
The account, push and sync settings moved to a new Accounts page in Preferences.
Times on the calendar are dimmer than titles and come after them, at the end of one-line entries, as in GNOME Calendar.
Upcoming shows in the sidebar only while some task has a due date, as Important does while some task has high priority.
A task dropped on the "Add a task" field no longer types its internal ID into it.
The window opens with the size it had when the app quit, and maximized if it was.

Tasks and events in your Nextcloud over CalDAV, kept in a local copy: the app works offline and syncs in the background, and push through WebDAV Push and ntfy brings changes from other devices within seconds.
Sign in through GNOME Online Accounts, in the browser (Nextcloud Login Flow), or with a login name and app password; passwords stay in the keyring.
Task lists: create, rename, recolour and delete them; categories as groups or tags with a sidebar filter; subtasks; manual order by drag and drop, shared with Nextcloud Tasks; sorting by due date.
Tasks: due dates and start times, priority, notes, several reminders each as desktop notifications with "Mark as Done", and an Upcoming page across lists.

A calendar with Month, Week and Agenda views: create, edit, move and delete events, repeating ones too (this occurrence, the following or all), with reminders. Weeks start on the day your region's formats say.
Time-blocking: drag tasks from "To Plan" onto an hour or a day, move and resize blocks in the week, drop them back to unplan.

Click an event or task on the calendar for its details, where an event's tasks and a task's subtasks can be ticked and added; double-click to edit it ("Edit on double click" in Preferences turns this off for instant details).
Tasks linked to events, and today's events at the top of Upcoming.
Search across tasks and events, undo with Ctrl+Z, keyboard shortcuts.
Preferences synced between devices through Nextcloud Files.
Runs in the background and starts with the session.
Translations into Polish, German, French, Spanish, Italian and Brazilian Portuguese, for the app and the extension. Polish is reviewed; the others are first drafts.
Packages for GNOME 49 and newer: a Flatpak bundle, a .deb for Ubuntu 26.04 and newer, a tarball for other distributions (both with the extension), and the extension as a zip.

A GNOME Shell extension: the open-task count in the top bar, and a menu with a task list, a month calendar with dots for what each day holds and the coming week's agenda; it adds tasks and events and opens the app where you click. Its options are in the app's Preferences. Without the app installed, its menu says so and links to the download.
